{{Quote|According to them, the place was once known as ''Kligson's Moon''&mdash;but because the mechanical genius who ''built'' it from space salvage insists on surrounding himself strictly with ''robots''&mdash;the few who ''know'' about this spot have come to call it&hellip; ''Droid World!''<nowiki></nowiki>|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], to [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]|<ref name="SW47" />}}
'''Kligson's Moon''', also known as '''Droid World''', was a massive mobile [[Space station/Legends|platform]] that served as a home for the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Kligson/Legends|Kligson]] and a large, bustling society of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. A popular [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] legend during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the "Droid World" was constructed out of spare parts after Kligson's rebuilding as a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]], and relocated to a remote location where organics were not permitted. Surprisingly fast and powerful for its unwieldy appearance, Kligson's Moon occasionally attracted visitors who were interested in Kligson's famed [[Technician/Legends|mechanical]] skill, and a visit by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] helped kick off a [[Kligson's Moon civil war|civil war]] aboard the station in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].

==Description==
{{Quote|You're ''talking'' to Kligson, Rebel! And I suffered enough in the ''Clone Wars'' to make me hostile to my fellow organics ''forever!'' I'm a ''cyborg,'' now, more machine than man;&hellip; and ''happy'' to cast my lot ''with'' the machines! Leave ''me'' and my Droid World in ''peace!''<nowiki></nowiki>|[[Kligson/Legends|Kligson]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="SW47" />}}
[[File:KligsonsMoon-MSW47.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Kligson's Moon.]]
A massive, mobile [[Space station/Legends|space platform]] created by the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[Technician/Legends|technician]] [[Kligson/Legends|Kligson]], Kligson's Moon&mdash;also known as the "[[Droid/Legends|Droid]] World"&mdash;contained its own wholly mechanical society of approximately 1,000 droids during the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Eight hundred [[Meter/Legends|meters]] long, Kligson's Moon was constructed out of spare parts, such as [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Hull/Legends|hulls]], drive [[Engine/Legends|engines]] and space station decks. However, its unwieldy and uneven appearance belied a surprising speed and power, and it boasted significant weaponry and [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielding]]. Kligson's Moon was outfitted with 30 [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] batteries and five [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor]] [[Tractor beam projector/Legends|projectors]], while still being large enough to hold 2,000 passengers and 5,000 metric tons of cargo.<ref name="CFTD" />

Not long after its construction, Kligson cultivated a thriving civilization of droids aboard his moon, with only two rules: no organics were allowed to set foot in his domain, and anything he repaired, he kept. Kligson was known as a master mechanic, and his station contained extensive facilities to assist in his work on droid design. This included a massive, open smelting pit that could melt even the toughest alloys, emanating from the tremendous heat generated by the station's core. Kligson himself oversaw all goings-on aboard his moon from a control station on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], from which he could hail approaching ships and direct all weapons systems.<ref name="SW47" />

==History==
{{Quote|I ''like'' a challenge, but my world has ''two rules'' that must be obeyed... The ''first'' is that no ''organic'' sets foot on Kligson's Moon. The ''second''&hellip; anything I repair, I ''keep!''<nowiki></nowiki>|[[Kligson/Legends|Kligson]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="SW47" />}}
After the end of the Clone Wars and the [[Declaration of a New Order]], Kligson&mdash;a lifelong warrior who had served in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]&mdash;took a post as an [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. However, when he refused to lead an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] conquest of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Sucharme]], he was swiftly betrayed, attacked and left for dead by the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] he commanded. His fellow patriots in the [[Grohl Liberation Front]] saved Kligson's life by outfitting him with a new, [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] body, hoping that their fellow Sucharmese native would help them fight off the Imperial advance. Instead, Kligson began to withdraw further and further from contact with fellow organics. Kligson used the [[Ostega Orbital Yards]] to build a massive space station out of discarded starship parts, one that was derisively dubbed "Kligsom's Moon" by members of the GLF. Rather than use the station to attack the Imperials, however, Kligson fired up its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] and disappeared, leaving the war behind.<ref name="EGWAC8" />

[[File:Bye.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kligson's moon enters hyperspace.]]
No longer comfortable in the company of organics, Kligson instead found solace in his fellow mechanicals, turning Kligson's Moon into a bustling haven for wayward droids.<ref name="SW47" /> By the time of the Galactic Civil War, the "Droid World" had become considered a myth, a tall tale shared by [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="CFTD" /> However, it was very real&mdash;and occasionally, as rumors of Kligson's technological mastery spread through [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], it attracted the odd organic visitor. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], that small list grew to include [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who tracked Kligson down in the hopes the cyborg could give them a full schematic of a new [[Imperial warbot]] that had begun to threaten Rebel forces in ground engagements.<ref name="SW47" />

However, Kligson's chief [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]]&mdash;a rejected Imperial [[Z-X3 experimental droid trooper|battle droid prototype]] called "[[Z-X3|Zee-Exthree]]"&mdash;secretly had gathered a [[Z-X3's faction|faction]] of Imperial-aligned droids, and the arrival of the the Rebels proved a signal to Zee-Exthree and his compatriots to launch their [[Kligson's Moon civil war|coup attempt]] to overthrow Kligson and seize his moon in the Empire's name. However, Kligson suspected the droid's treachery, and outsmarted and outmaneuvered Zee-Exthree, using the reconstructed warbot to defeat his enemies in a brief war that tore the moon apart. Afterwards, fearing attention from the Empire, Kligson ignited his station's engines again and relocated it deeper into space.<ref name="SW47" />

Kligson's Moon once again became little more than a story after its relocation, and it was quite some time before any outsider discovered the Droid World's new location.<ref name="CFTD" /> Kligson's Moon later came under [[Attack on Kligson's Moon|attack]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], when the [[Anti-droid sentiment/Legends|technophobic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invaders attempted to destroy the station. However, the group of [[Shard (species)|Shard]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] known as the [[Iron Knight]]s fought off the Yuuzhan Vong and saved Kligson's Moon.<ref name="DTF" />

==Behind the scenes==
Kligson's Moon first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 47|''Star Wars'' (1977) 47]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and released in [[1981]]. In the comic, the station was illustrated by [[Carmine Infantino]],<ref name="SW47" /> and it was additionally portrayed by [[Dick Foes]] in the book-and-record ''[[The Further Adventures: Droid World]]''.<ref name="further">''[[The Further Adventures: Droid World]]''</ref>
